body.statement: Every symbolic formula returned by \(\operatorname{Branch\text{-}sCIDP}(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) equals \(\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)\) for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\). The role graph has at most \(2^{|X\cup C|}\) states, every nonrepeating trace has length at most \(2^{|X\cup C|}-1\), and the shared formula DAG can be constructed in \(O(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\mathrm{form}})\) symbolic operations. No implication from \(\operatorname{AllFail}\) to nonidentification is asserted here.
body.justification: Exhaustive legal exchanges preserve the target and isolate the converse difficulty without sacrificing a usable positive identification procedure.
body.gap: Chen--Mooij prove soundness for their conditional procedure; the branch closure and shared-cache accounting are not stated as this explicit formula-search theorem.
body.consumer: PAGId can return selected-cohort formulas with a finite auditable role trace even before a complete failure theorem is available.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an arbitrary represented model \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\) and assignments \(x\), \(c\), and \(y\) in the finite support spaces declared in the target.  For every \(A\subseteq V\), put
\[
 \mathcal X_A(\mathbf M)
 :=\prod_{v\in A}\operatorname{supp}_{\mathbf M}(V_v),
\]
with \(\mathcal X_{\varnothing}(\mathbf M)\) equal to the singleton containing the empty assignment.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}disjoint\text{-}query\text{-}sets}\) makes the assignment \(a\in\mathcal X_W(\mathbf M)\), defined by \(a_X=x\) and \(a_C=c\), well defined.  At a role state \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\), write \(\bar x=a_{\bar X}\) and \(\bar c=a_{\bar C}\), and define the proof-local conditional kernel
\[
 K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)
 :=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),
 \bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1\right).
 \tag{1}
\]
The sets in (1) are pairwise compatible: the definition of a role state gives \(\bar X\mathbin{\dot\cup}\bar C=W=X\cup C\), while \(Y\cap W=\varnothing\) follows from \(\mathrm{ass{:}disjoint\text{-}query\text{-}sets}\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}discrete\text{-}selected\text{-}model}\), the finite selected stratum used in (1) has positive mass at every assignment under consideration; explicitly,
\[
 P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 \bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1
 \mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x)\right)>0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus every conditional probability and every division below is defined, including the boundary case \(\bar C=\varnothing\).

We first prove invariance along the role-state graph.  At its root \(\rho_0=(X,C)\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}query}\) gives
\[
 K_{\rho_0,\mathbf M}(y)
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c,S=\mathbf 1)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c).
 \tag{3}
\]
Consider an edge that moves a nonempty current bucket intersection \(T\subseteq\bar X\) from treatment to conditioning.  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}reachable\text{-}role\text{-}graph}\) includes this edge only when the corresponding Rule--2 separation holds.  Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}selected\text{-}rule\text{-}two}\) with
\[
 A_0=Y,\qquad B_0=T,\qquad C_0=\bar C,
 \qquad D_0=\bar X\setminus T.
\]
These four sets are pairwise disjoint by the role partition and \(Y\cap W=\varnothing\).  Using the restrictions of \(a\) on both sides of the Rule--2 equality yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 K_{(\bar X,\bar C),\mathbf M}(y)
 &=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y=y\mid \bar C=\bar c,
 \operatorname{do}(T=a_T,\bar X\setminus T=a_{\bar X\setminus T}),
 S=\mathbf 1\right)\\
 &=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y=y\mid T=a_T,\bar C=\bar c,
 \operatorname{do}(\bar X\setminus T=a_{\bar X\setminus T}),
 S=\mathbf 1\right)\\
 &=K_{(\bar X\setminus T,\,\bar C\cup T),\mathbf M}(y).
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
If instead an edge moves a nonempty \(T\subseteq\bar C\) from conditioning to treatment, apply the same lemma with
\[
 A_0=Y,\qquad B_0=T,\qquad C_0=\bar C\setminus T,
 \qquad D_0=\bar X.
\]
Reading its equality from right to left gives
\[
 K_{(\bar X,\bar C),\mathbf M}(y)
 =K_{(\bar X\cup T,\,\bar C\setminus T),\mathbf M}(y).
 \tag{5}
\]
Induction on the finite length of any directed trace from \(\rho_0\), using (3)--(5), proves
\[
 K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)=\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)
 \quad\text{for every reachable role state }\rho.
 \tag{6}
\]

Suppose now that Branch-sCIDP succeeds at \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\).  Its terminal sIDP call has outcome set \(A_0=Y\cup\bar C\) and intervention set \(B_0=\bar X\).  They are disjoint, and \(A_0\neq\varnothing\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}nonempty\text{-}outcome}\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}soundness}\), applied directly on the published positive discrete class \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\), therefore gives, pointwise for every \(y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)\),
\[
 F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 =J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y',\bar c;\bar x).
 \tag{7}
\]
This is not an inference from the rational binary certificate subclass.  Summing (7) over the full finite outcome support and using the definition of \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
 F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 &=\sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
 J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y',\bar c;\bar x)\\
 &=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 \bar C=\bar c\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),S=\mathbf 1\right)\\
 &=D_{\rho,\mathbf M}(\bar c;\bar x)>0,
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
where the last inequality follows from (2) and the positive selected-intervention normalizer.  Dividing (7) by (8), applying the definition of conditional probability, and then applying (6), we obtain
\[
 \frac{F_\rho(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})}
 {\sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
 F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})}
 =K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c).
 \tag{9}
\]
Thus the normalized returned expression is an observed-law identifying map for the causal target.  Its equality with the target has been derived from Rule--2 invariance and sIDP soundness, rather than imposed by definition.

It remains to prove the finite-search and cache bounds.  A role state is uniquely determined by \(\bar X\subseteq W\), since \(\bar C=W\setminus\bar X\).  Hence
\[
 |\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)|\leq 2^{|W|}=2^{|X\cup C|}.
 \tag{10}
\]
A trace with no repeated state and \(r\) visited states has \(r-1\) edges, so (10) gives the asserted upper bound \(2^{|X\cup C|}-1\) on its length.

At each visited state, the outer enumeration tests at most two directions for each of at most \(n\) buckets.  Each relevant manipulated graph has polynomial size in \(n\).  A Rule--2 separation test is decided by a finite reachability search over its admissible edge-incidence states; bucket formation, anterior closure, and region formation are also graph searches of polynomial size.  Consequently all outer role-state work is
\[
 O\!\left(2^n\operatorname{poly}(n)\right).
 \tag{11}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}recursion\text{-}structure}\), a deterministic BuildTree subproblem is keyed by one region \(R\subseteq V\), and a fixing subproblem is keyed by one pair \(R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\).  There are \(2^n\) keys of the first kind and
\[
 \#\{(R,T_0):R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\}
 =\sum_{T_0\subseteq V}2^{|T_0|}
 =(1+2)^n=3^n
 \tag{12}
\]
keys of the second kind.  The final equality follows directly by assigning each vertex independently to \(R\), to \(T_0\setminus R\), or to \(V\setminus T_0\).  The same recursion lemma states that BuildTree descends only to proper region children and that every successful fixing iteration removes a nonempty bucket.  Therefore each deterministic key terminates.  Under Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}shared\text{-}formula\text{-}cache}\), it is evaluated at most once and incurs only \(\operatorname{poly}(n)\) graph work.  Equations (11) and (12) thus bound all cached graph computation by
\[
 O\!\left(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)\right).
 \tag{13}
\]
Each marginalization, product, quotient, and assembly operation contributes a constant-arity node to the shared formula DAG.  Constructing and emitting those nodes costs \(O(L_{\mathrm{form}})\) by the definition of \(L_{\mathrm{form}}\).  Combining this output cost with (13) proves
\[
 O\!\left(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\mathrm{form}}\right).
\]
The proof invoked sIDP soundness only after a terminal call succeeded.  It therefore gives no implication from \(\operatorname{AllFail}\) to nonidentification, exactly as claimed.
